html:
The Pawnee Nation of Oklahoma is the government of the Pawnee people, with its centre at Pawnee in northern Oklahoma. The map shows its land in 1492, but the Pawnee only moved there in the 1870s.

In 1492 the ancestors of the Pawnee lived along the Platte and Loup rivers in what is now Nebraska. They spoke a Caddoan language, related to those of the Arikara, the Wichita and the Caddo. They lived in large earth lodges, farmed maize, beans and squash, and went on long bison hunts twice a year. Their star lore guided their farming and their villages.

Disease and attacks by the Lakota cut their numbers in the 1800s, and many Pawnee men served as scouts for the US Army. In 1874 and 1875 they gave up their last Nebraska land and moved to Indian Territory. See also Pawnee.
